title: Unencrypted GPS Transmission
description: Child's device (EE2) transmits live GPS coordinates to the backend (P1) without encryption, exposing sensitive location data.
assumptions: Device capabilities and network security posture are assumed sufficient to transmit raw GPS data.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: Backend (P1) receives and stores the unencrypted GPS coordinates from the child device (EE2), creating a data flow where sensitive location data is processed and potentially stored.
assumptions: Backend system is assumed to have appropriate security controls to prevent unauthorized access or leakage.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The backend process (P1) writes location pings to the Location History Store (DS1). This constitutes a direct transfer of personal data from a process to a data store, which is a valid interaction type. The threat is grounded in the explicit transfer of data across the boundary defined by the flow.
assumptions: The data being transferred is personal location data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Location History Store (DS1) receives location pings from the backend process (P1). This is a valid interaction where a data store receives data from a process. The threat is grounded in the explicit transfer of data across the boundary defined by the flow.
assumptions: The data being received is personal location data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) forwards new location pings to the Geofencing Engine (P2). This constitutes a data disclosure as P1 transfers personal location data to a third-party process (P2) for processing.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) receives and processes location pings from P1. This is a data disclosure as P2 processes personal location data from a third-party process (P1).

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: A malicious actor could potentially access the Family Account Store (DS2) and extract the configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) intended for the Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2). This constitutes a Low severity threat where the data store is the originator of the flow.
assumptions: The Family Account Store contains sensitive user location preferences that are not intended to be shared externally.

title: Unauthorized Data Exfiltration
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) could potentially access the Family Account Store (DS2) to read the zone definitions. This is a Medium severity threat where the process is the originator of the flow.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine has direct read access to the Family Account Store configuration.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: An external entity (EE1) may attempt to access or manipulate the geofencing data flow (P2) without proper authorization, potentially leading to unauthorized location data exposure.
assumptions: The system allows external entities to interact with the process without explicit permission checks.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific threat type 'L' (Unauthorized Access) is the most appropriate classification for this interaction type, as the context suggests a push notification flow rather than a direct data access flow.

title: Data Leakage to External Entity
description: The parent external entity (EE1) may leak or expose the geofencing data flow (P2) to unauthorized parties, potentially violating privacy policies.
assumptions: The external entity has the capability to interact with the process but lacks the necessary controls to prevent data leakage.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific threat type 'D' (Data Leakage) is the most appropriate classification for this interaction type, as the context suggests a push notification flow rather than a direct data access flow.

title: Data Leakage
description: Parent (ExternalEntity) registers an account, creating a child profile. The child's sensitive personal data (name, DOB, school) is stored in the Mobile App Backend (Process). This flow represents a direct data flow from an external entity to a process, where sensitive personal information is being collected and stored.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: The Mobile App Backend (Process) receives the parent's account registration and the child's sensitive personal data (name, DOB, school). This process is storing and potentially exposing this data to unauthorized parties.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The backend process (P1) transfers account, child profile, and geofence zone data to the Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process explicitly transfers personal data across a boundary to a data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data store (DS2) receives and stores account, child profile, and geofence zone data from the backend process (P1). This represents a data disclosure as the store is the recipient of personal data.

title: Unauthorized Location Access
description: Parent (ExternalEntity) requests to view child's current location or history on a map without explicit consent or authorization.
assumptions: Parent entity has access to the map data but lacks the specific permission to retrieve location details.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Process P1 (Mobile App Backend) discloses sensitive location data (current location or history) to the Parent (ExternalEntity) without a secure, authenticated channel.
assumptions: The backend process is exposed to the external entity's request.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) accesses stored location history (DS1) without explicit authorization or encryption, potentially exposing sensitive user location data.
assumptions: Assumption: The backend application has the necessary permissions to read the data store.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain: The specific authorization model for the backend access is not fully detailed in the provided context.

title: Inappropriate Data Exposure
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) exposes location history data to an external entity (the parent's map/history view) without proper data masking or filtering, violating the principle of least privilege.
assumptions: Assumption: The parent's view is not configured with data masking capabilities.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain: The specific data masking configuration for the parent's view is not detailed in the provided context.

title: Unauthorized Location Sharing
description: Parent (EE1) initiates a data flow to a Process (P1) to share location data with a secondary guardian. This action is triggered by the parent's intent to invite a relative, creating a privacy risk where location data is exposed to an unauthorized third party.
assumptions: The parent has the authority to share location data with a secondary guardian.

title: Location Data Exposure
description: The data flow from the Parent (EE1) to the Mobile App Backend (P1) transmits location data. This data-centric threat arises at the data flow itself, where the transmission of location information to a third-party process (the guardian) could be intercepted, logged, or used to identify the parties involved.
assumptions: The mobile app backend processes and transmits the location data to the external entity.

title: Unauthorized Access to Secondary Guardian
description: Process P1 grants access to ExternalEntity EE3, which is an external system. This interaction is valid under the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity), but the specific action of sharing live location data with an external entity without explicit authorization or encryption could constitute a privacy risk if the external entity is not a trusted partner.
assumptions: The secondary guardian (EE3) is an external system that should be trusted but is not explicitly defined as such in the DFD.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the secondary guardian is considered a 'trusted' external entity in the context of this DFD. If it is, the threat is mitigated; if not, it is a privacy risk.

title: Unauthorized Access from Process P1
description: ExternalEntity EE3 receives data from Process P1. If EE3 is not a trusted external entity, it may be vulnerable to unauthorized access from P1, which is a valid interaction (Process->ExternalEntity).
assumptions: EE3 is an external system. If it is not a trusted partner, it is vulnerable to unauthorized access.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if EE3 is a trusted external entity. If it is, the threat is mitigated; if not, it is a privacy risk.

title: Data Leakage
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics are shared with an external advertising/analytics partner, potentially exposing sensitive user data.
assumptions: The partner has access to the raw or aggregated data flows.

title: Data Leakage
description: The advertising/analytics partner may access or misuse the shared aggregated usage and engagement analytics.
assumptions: The partner has access to the data.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Child (ExternalEntity) sends a manual check-in / SOS message with their current location to the parent (Process). This message is attributed to the user (EE2) and constitutes non-repudiable data evidence of their location.
assumptions: The message is successfully transmitted and stored.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Mobile App Backend (Process) receives and stores a manual check-in / SOS message with the Child's current location. This data is attributed to the user (EE2) and constitutes non-repudiable data evidence of their location.
assumptions: The message is successfully transmitted and stored.
